grounding_notice: General Knowledge Mode: Material synthesized from foundational domain principles.

concepts.title: 1. Galileo's Insight & Inertia (First Law)
concepts.explanation_focus: Transition from Aristotelian intuition to Galileo's inclined planes and Newton's definition of inertia.
concepts.analogy: Slamming the brakes in a bus: passengers lurch forward because their bodies possess inertia.
concepts.visual_title: Newton's 1st Law: Net Force = 0 => Constant Velocity

checkpoint_question.question: When a car makes a sharp left turn, why do passengers feel thrown toward the right?
options: A mysterious centrifugal force pushes them outward.
Their body inertia wants to continue moving straight ahead while the car turns left.
The car's engine generates rightward momentum.
Gravity tilts to the right side.

misconception_traps.0: Invented force misconception: Attributing inertia to an active outward push.

concepts.title: 2. The Mathematical Engine: F = dp/dt = m*a (Second Law)
concepts.explanation_focus: Rate of change of momentum, relation to acceleration, unit of Newton (kg*m/s^2).
concepts.analogy: Pushing an empty shopping cart vs. pushing a cart stacked with heavy bricks.
concepts.visual_title: F_net = m * a  |  1 N = 1 kg * m/s²

checkpoint_question.question: If you double the net force applied to a mass while cutting its mass in half, by what factor does acceleration change?
checkpoint_question.sample_answer: Acceleration increases by a factor of 4 (a = 2F / (0.5m) = 4 * (F/m)).
checkpoint_question.rubric: Mathematical deduction using a = F/m resulting in 4x.

misconception_traps.2: Forgetting that halving mass also doubles acceleration.

concepts.title: 3. Gravitational Equality & Free Fall Misconception
concepts.explanation_focus: Why a bowling ball and a feather drop at identical rates in a vacuum despite different masses.
concepts.analogy: Galileo at the Leaning Tower of Pisa and Apollo 15 hammer-feather drop on the Moon.
concepts.visual_title: Free Fall in Vacuum: a = (m*g) / m = g (Identical for all masses)

checkpoint_question.question: Why does a 10 kg iron ball experience 10 times more gravitational force than a 1 kg ball, yet both accelerate at the exact same rate?
checkpoint_question.sample_answer: Because the 10 kg ball also has 10 times more inertia (resistance to acceleration), so the extra force is perfectly balanced by the extra mass (a = F/m).
checkpoint_question.rubric: Must mention that greater force is countered by proportionally greater inertia/mass.

concepts.title: 4. Action-Reaction Pairs: Rockets & Earth Recoil (Third Law)
concepts.explanation_focus: Simultaneous paired forces on distinct bodies. Rocket propulsion mechanics.
concepts.analogy: A rocket expelling hot exhaust gas downward; the gas pushes the rocket upward into space.

checkpoint_question.question: When a small mosquito collides with the windshield of a speeding truck, which force is greater?
options: The truck exerts a much larger force on the mosquito than the mosquito exerts on the truck.
The forces exerted by the mosquito and truck on each other are exactly equal in magnitude.
The mosquito exerts a larger force because it decelerates faster.
It depends on the relative speed of the mosquito.
checkpoint_question.rubric: Newton's 3rd Law equality of force magnitudes regardless of mass asymmetry.

misconception_traps.0: Damage-force conflation: Confusing resulting acceleration/damage with the magnitude of the mutual interaction force.
